Strictly preserve his original facial features, hairstyle, body proportions and accessories.
<Subject 2> is the old Half-Moon Bay wharf in <Picture 2>, a stone slipway running down into the water with green moss in its seams, a row of dark iron bollards along the top, a dozen wooden fishing boats moored with blue paint flaking off grey timber, and a two-storey grey stone house on the right with a concrete lamp post. <Subject 2> defines spatial layout and environmental continuity.
Spatial anchor for this clip: the narrow gangway plank runs out from the stone slipway over green water, the boy at its head with the hemp sack on his shoulder and the two idlers blocking its far end.

detailed_description
cool desaturated palette with warm amber accents, 35mm film texture with subtle grain, motivated practical lighting

[Shot 1] Carrying straight on from the light change at the end of the previous shot, a medium shot from the front at eye level, the camera tracking slowly at his side on <Subject 2>. Noon sun falls straight down on the slipway with <Subject 1> standing at its head, the empty hemp sack over one shoulder and his body turned toward the narrow plank; behind him a dozen wooden fishing boats lie nose-out along the crescent harbour with blue paint flaking off grey timber, and a two-storey grey stone house closes the shore. He shifts the sack on his shoulder and puts one foot on the plank. His eyes narrow against the glare, his mouth sets into a single line, his jaw works once. High noon light drops from directly overhead and blows the wet stone white, with his shadow short and black under his feet. His cloth shoe lands on the plank with a hollow thud and the boards give a low creak under him.
[Shot 2] At 00:02.500, the camera cuts to a close-up from the side from a low angle, the camera pushing in at medium speed. <Subject 1> walks two steps along the narrow plank with the hemp sack bouncing at his back, the plank no wider than one man and the green water sliding under its edges. He takes the steps one at a time, the sack swinging with each stride, his forearms loose at his sides. His eyelids stay low, the muscle at his jaw sits corded, his breathing stays even and shallow. High noon light from above lays along the top of the plank and lets the water below go dark and green. His cloth shoe presses the boards with a dull thump and the timber groans under his weight.
[Shot 3] At 00:04.400, the camera cuts to a medium close-up over the shoulder from eye level, held static with the frame shaking slightly, with <Subject 1>'s shoulder and the empty sack soft in the near edge of the frame. Two village idlers stand blocking the head of the plank, the one on the left short and thick through the chest in a faded blue wraparound shirt with his arms folded tight, the one on the right tall and loose-limbed in a stained grey shirt with his weight cocked on one hip; the sack swings out as <Subject 1> checks his step and the pair of them deliberately swing their shoulders into his path. The short one's mouth corners tip up, the tall one's eyes crease with a held-back laugh, both their chins come up together. Noon light from above and behind them rims their shoulders while their faces sit in shadow. One of them lets a laugh out through his nose and a cloth shoe scrapes the plank edge beside him.
[Shot 4] At 00:06.200, the camera cuts to a close-up from a three-quarter side at ground level, held static, showing only his feet and the plank. The heel of his cloth shoe comes down past the edge of the boards and finds nothing; the top half of his body drops away to the side, the sack cloth pulling taut across his back as the weight goes out from under him. The wet streak along the plank edge and the churn of green water below fill the rest of the frame. The sack's hemp rasping loud across his back, over a wave knocking the piles somewhere under the boards.
[Shot 5] At 00:07.300, the camera cuts to a medium close-up from the front from a slight high angle, the camera pushing in fast. <Subject 1> pitches sideways off the plank with both arms flung wide, the face turned up at the lens for one beat before he is gone, the empty sack tangled across his back; the water opens and throws a sheet of white spray up into the frame. His eyelids snap open, his mouth pulls into a hollow, his jaw line drags straight. From above, noon sun drives down onto the white water while the slipway behind him burns out bright. The water bursts with a heavy slap, and his shoe scrapes hard across the boards as he goes.
[Shot 6] At 00:08.600, the camera cuts to an extreme close-up from above, held static. Rings of white water run out across the surface one after another from the point where he went in, the edges of the slipway and two grey faces leaning over the top of the frame filling the rest. From above, noon light lays flat on the rings and lets the water go flat grey-green under them. The rings hiss and slap out across the surface, under the drift of voices along the quay behind.
[Shot 7] At 00:10.000, the camera cuts to a close-up from the side from a low angle, held static, the two idlers framed low against the bright sky. The short one and the tall one look at each other once and then turn and walk away up the quay with their hands swinging loose; the empty sack lies where it was knocked down across the boards. The short one's eyelid comes up, the tall one's mouth tips sideways, both noses let out a short breath. From below, the noon glare off the water blows out their outlines while their faces drop into shadow. Their shoes clack along the boards and the sack drops flat with a dull knock. Across the last of this shot every other sound on the quay is swallowed up by the water and the noise cuts out flat.
